correctness.rationale: The full published facet theorem applies for b1>=2. The scalar inradius and unique uniform incenter follow by matching every lower facet to each upper subset inequality at Euclidean distance r. Distinct minimizing cardinalities k!=l force (k+sqrt(k))/(l+sqrt(l)) rational; algebra forces both perfect squares. For any selection of square indices, define integer A_j near M(j+sqrt(j)) with M=100n^4, with normalized equality precisely on the chosen squares. For a nonsquare singleton, an additional n+4 integer increment off target forces unique minimal excess. The strict negative second difference of M(j+sqrt(j)) dominates all at-most-n+4 perturbations; reversed first differences are positive integral b_i with b1>=2, and telescoping recovers exactly the A_j. Binomial facet multiplicities give the maximum contact formula. Standard-library checker tested 431 patterns and 9605 exact separation comparisons, plus positivity/telescoping, which corroborate but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete realization and exclusion theorem for simultaneous facet tangencies is a natural geometric degeneracy classification for an infinite class of simple lattice polytopes. The perfect-square resonance is an arithmetic obstruction invisible in the face lattice, and the explicit integer-concavity construction realizes arbitrarily many prescribed active orbits in increasing dimensions. The sharp maximum number of tangencies is an invariant optimization over the integral parameter family. Previous scalar radius and singleton realization results do not subsume this classification.
